claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First of all, could you please tell me how many children you would like to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - his name is Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! It's lovely to meet you. Let me ask a few questions about Alex to help determine your eligibility.

How old is Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you. And does Alex live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't live with me currently.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Could you tell me a bit more about Alex's living situation? For example:

- Is Alex living with another family member or someone else?
- Is Alex in hospital or in local authority care?
- Or is there another arrangement?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives with his mum - my ex-partner.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for explaining. Since Alex lives with his mum, I have a couple more questions:

Are you currently contributing towards Alex's upkeep? For example, do you pay maintenance or contribute financially towards his care at a rate that is at least equal to the Child Benefit amount (currently £26.05 per week for the eldest or only child)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do contribute financially towards Alex. I help out with things like clothes, school supplies, and other expenses for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To clarify, do your financial contributions amount to at least £26.05 per week (which is the current Child Benefit rate for a first child)?

Also, is Alex's mum (your ex-partner) already claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Yes, my contributions are at least £26.05 per week - I make sure I'm helping out with what he needs.

As for whether his mum is claiming Child Benefit for Alex, I'm not entirely sure to be honest. Is that something I need to check?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Yes, it would be important to find out whether Alex's mum is already claiming Child Benefit for him. This is because **only one person can receive Child Benefit for a child** at any one time.

Based on the information you've provided:
- You are contributing financially towards Alex's upkeep at a rate of at least £26.05 per week

This means you could potentially qualify for Child Benefit for Alex, even though he doesn't live with you, **but only if no one else is already claiming it for him**.

Here's what you should know:
- If Alex's mum is already claiming Child Benefit for him, you would not be able to receive it as well
- If neither of you is currently claiming, you could potentially claim it since you're contributing towards his upkeep
- If you both want to claim, you would need to agree between yourselves who should receive it. If you can't agree, HMRC will decide

Could you check with Alex's mum whether she is already claiming Child Benefit for him? This will help me give you a clearer answer about your eligibility.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, I see. Well, his mum isn't claiming Child Benefit for Alex - she's not getting it for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. That's helpful information.

I have just a couple more questions to complete the eligibility check:

Do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. And one final question:

Is Alex in approved education, or is he simply at primary school given his age (8 years old)? I just want to confirm he's not in any form of paid work or receiving certain benefits in his own right - though I appreciate this is very unlikely at his age!

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's just at primary school - nothing unusual there. He's not working or getting any benefits himself, he's just a regular 8-year-old at school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming all of that. I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me summarise your situation:

- You live in the UK (Manchester)
- Alex is 8 years old and attends primary school
- Alex lives with his mum (your ex-partner)
- You contribute at least £26.05 per week towards Alex's upkeep
- Alex's mum is not currently claiming Child Benefit for him
- Alex is not working or receiving any benefits himself

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm pleased to tell you that **you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

✅ **You live in the UK** – This is a basic requirement for Child Benefit.

✅ **Alex is under 16** – At 8 years old, he qualifies as an eligible child.

✅ **You contribute towards Alex's upkeep** – Even though Alex doesn't live with you, you're contributing at least £26.05 per week towards his care (such as clothes, school supplies, and other expenses). This meets the requirement of paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards looking after him.

✅ **No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex** – Since his mum isn't claiming, there's no conflict. Only one person can receive Child Benefit for a child at any one time.

You can proceed to make a claim for Child Benefit. If you do claim successfully, just be aware that you'll need to continue contributing towards Alex's upkeep at the same rate to remain eligible.

Is there anything else you'd like to know?
